title: Senior Director at Capgemini Sees TCS Gaining Share Through Aggressive Pricing, With AI Margins Likely to Compress
expert: Senior Director at Capgemini (competitor; bid against TCS on multi-year deals above $5 million); interview 2026-11-04
verdict: A Capgemini senior director lost a large bank deal to TCS, which bid 12%–14% margins on multi-year deals above $5 million vs his firm's 20%+ target: TCS is buying share at thin deal margins.

EBIT margin and the 25% exit: 🔴 TCS bid 12%–14% margins vs 20%+ at the competitor on multi-year deals above $5 million (first-hand), fitting 2QFY27 EBIT 24.0%, -120bp y/y (SB #62837). → Tenet 2 (EBIT ~24%) ↑ {c6}
🟡 AI-led work earns 25%–35% margins, an 18%–25% premium (estimate), in line with mgmt's higher-margin AI (SB #62847), but expected to compress as it commoditizes. → Tenet 2 (EBIT ~24%) → {c8}
Non-AI revenue trend: 🔴 Clients demand 15%–25% efficiency at application-maintenance renewals; 60% of savings returned to their P&L (estimate) vs mgmt "no pricing pressure" (SB #62847): conflicting. → Tenet 1 (AI deflates core) ↑ {c11}
🔴 AI deals carry smaller teams and deal sizes, so AI revenue may not replace traditional scale; consistent with non-AI -1.5% q/q (SB #62834). → Tenet 1 (AI deflates core) ↑ {c10}
TCV / book-to-bill and BFSI momentum: 🟡 Outcome-based ~30% of deals today, ~50% within 1 to 18 months; ~20% of relationships reviewed every 3 to 5 years (estimates); first read. → Tenet 3 (order intake) → {c16}
🔴 Infosys and HCL bid as low as 10% or 11% (hearsay) to undercut TCS. → Tenet 5 (competition) ↑ {c8}

changes: Deal margins 12%–14% (first-hand) vs company EBIT 24.0%, -120bp y/y in 2QFY27 (SB #62837): consistent with margin pressure.
AI margin premium 18%–25% vs mgmt "AI revenues at higher margins than company average" (SB #62847): consistent.
Renewal efficiency demands 15%–25% vs mgmt "no pricing pressure" (SB #62847): conflicting.
Subcontractors kept for niche skills and visas for one to two years vs subcon 6.8% of sales, +190bp y/y (SB #62837): consistent.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (AI deflates the non-AI core): ↑ — 15%–25% renewal efficiency demands with 60% returned to clients; AI deals smaller.
Tenet 2 (EBIT stays near 24%): ↑ — TCS wins at 12%–14% deal margins vs 20%+ at peers.
Tenet 3 (order intake): → — share gains at low margins support TCV, but ~20% of relationships face review every 3 to 5 years.
Tenet 5 (competition): ↑ — Infosys/HCL bid 10%–11%; GCCs and niche players take share.
